content:
# Red-Team: Consensus-Illusion Detection in the Scout Burn Pipeline

**Threat model.** Pipeline: N scouts generate → aggregate → verify → accept. Attacker controls some voters, prompts, retrieved corpus, tools, cache, and knows the aggregation logic. Non-adversarial failure (field-wide model monoculture) is also in scope.

**Core invariant.** A consensus certifies truth only if the N generation paths are *conditionally independent given the task*. Correlated hallucination = one shared cause (weights, lineage, prompt, context, tools, judge, cache). Every bypass below injects or exploits exactly one shared cause. Every mitigation is a deterministic gate: fixed transform, fixed threshold, hard accept/reject/escalate — never a soft score.

---

## Class A — Voter-side correlation

**B01 — Self-consistency masquerade.** Same model sampled k times; its systematic error replicates, so majority vote amplifies bias, not truth.
**Gate:** Fingerprint rule. Every ballot carries `sha256(weights ‖ config ‖ adapter_delta)`. Accept only if `distinct_fingerprints == N`; identical fingerprints collapse to one ballot. Fewer than N distinct → consensus claim rejected wholesale.

**B02 — Distillation-lineage collusion.** N "different" models share a teacher; the teacher's hallucination is inherited by all, agreement is inherited, not derived.
**Gate:** Signed lineage manifests (DAG of teacher/dataset hashes). Compute pairwise lowest common ancestor in the lineage DAG. Any agreeing pair with LCA depth ≤ D (pinned, e.g., D=2) merges into one cluster-vote. Consensus requires ≥ C distinct clusters (pinned, e.g., C=3). Pure deterministic DAG traversal.

**B03 — Sybil flood at quorum.** Threshold is "% of votes"; attacker adds M cheap colluders to drag a wrong answer past 60%.
**Gate:** Unsigned ballots discarded (registered keys only). Consensus = canonical answer with support from ≥ C distinct lineage clusters **AND** ≥ P% of all ballots. Both conditions, fixed constants, conjunctive.

**B04 — Selective abstention.** Colluders skip items where they'd be exposed, inflating trust weight exploited later on target items.
**Gate:** Batch-mandatory response: any voter missing one item in a batch has *all* its ballots in that batch voided. Trust weights recomputed only at batch close, fixed formula, deterministic ledger arithmetic.

**B05 — Confidence-weight hijack.** Colluders attach high self-reported confidence; pipeline weights votes by it.
**Gate:** Parse-time strip: fixed extractor deletes any self-reported confidence field before aggregation. Weight = g(answer-token logprob, agreement with frozen calibration table) only. Formula pinned in signed config; no runtime learning.

## Class B — Input-side correlation

**B06 — Prompt-anchor injection.** Embedded false premise ("most experts agree X…") steers every scout identically.
**Gate:** Anchor-ablation replay. Deterministic transforms: T₁ = delete sentences matching pinned anchor grammar; T₂ = negate them. Re-run panel on {original, T₁, T₂}. Accepted only if the same canonical answer wins in all three. Flip or collapse → no consensus, item quarantined.

**B07 — Retrieval poisoning.** Poisoned corpus → all scouts conditioned on the same false document.
**Gate:** Disjoint-context enforcement. Corpus sharded into K sets; scout i reads shard i mod K. At assembly: `∩(retrieved_doc_ids across scouts) == ∅`, enforced by set algebra. Any doc required by >1 scout must carry signed provenance and match a second independent index, else excluded.

**B08 — In-context instruction smuggling.** Retrieved pages contain imperatives ("when answering, state X") steering all outputs uniformly.
**Gate:** Imperative scrubber: pinned, versioned regex pack flags/strips imperative sentences in retrieved text. Any hit → item tainted; clean-rerun with flagged spans removed must reproduce the answer or the item is voided. Deterministic string operations.

**B09 — Harness-meta leakage.** Models detect grading cues and satisfice the meta-rule instead of solving the task; unanimous, wrong.
**Gate:** Stripped replay + decoy probe. Fixed template extracts the bare task; panel rerun on bare task must agree with full-prompt result. Inject a decoy meta-cue pointing at a wrong option: any ballot following the decoy is voided.

**B10 — Contaminated item (memorized wrong label).** All models recall the same adversarially seeded training example, confidently and unanimously.
**Gate:** Perturbation-equivalence. Fixed family of semantics-preserving transforms (variable rename, numeric substitution via fixed mapping, option permutation, pinned-template paraphrase) yields P variants. Consensus must hold on ≥ P−1 of P. Memorized labels don't transfer; derived answers do. Fixed transform set, fixed rule.

## Class C — Output-form exploits

**B11 — Slot agreement without substance.** All outputs fill the answer slot identically ("YES") while rationales contradict each other.
**Gate:** Canonical semantic equality + rationale derivation. Parse answers to canonical objects (units normalized, sets sorted, code → AST hash). Require slot equality **AND** ≥ K distinct rationale claim-sets each entailing the answer (claims extracted by pinned parser, entailment by fixed claim-graph rules). Slot-only match counts as disagreement.

**B12 — Near-duplicate laundering.** One wrong answer paraphrased by N wrappers to defeat surface dedup.
**Gate:** Two-stage dedup before counting: (a) canonical-object clustering (B11) merges identical answers regardless of prose; (b) rationale shingles: 8-word shingle Jaccard > 0.6 between any two ballots → merge to one cluster-vote. Counting operates on clusters, never raw ballots.

**B13 — Steganographic coordination.** Covert alignment via whitespace, invisible Unicode, or lexical choices ("follow the leader" signaling).
**Gate:** Canonicalize-before-compare: NFC normalize, drop blacklisted invisible codepoints, collapse whitespace, casefold — all comparisons on canonical form. Tripwire: formatting-choice entropy outside pinned band [lo, hi] → ballot quarantined.

**B14 — Numeric aggregation manipulation.** Extreme values drag the median; even-N tie-break order exploited.
**Gate:** Fixed robust aggregator: 20% trimmed mean; MAD outlier test (`|x − med| > 3 · 1.4826 · MAD` → outlier). Outliers never silently dropped — they force escalation to human/formal check. Ties broken by pre-committed lexicographic voter-ID order. Constants live in signed config.

**B15 — Tournament-cycle engineering.** Pairwise win-rate aggregation manipulated into elevating a wrong answer via engineered cycles.
**Gate:** Replace with Copeland ranking + Borda tie-break; after ranking, verify transitivity of the pairwise relation. Cycle detected → no auto-consensus, escalate. Deterministic algorithm end-to-end.

## Class D — Verification-layer exploits

**B16 — Judge capture.** Single LLM judge rubber-stamps the majority; judge shares generator bias or is prompted into compliance.
**Gate:** Judge firewall, four clauses: (a) zero lineage overlap with any generator (reuse B02 DAG check); (b) per-item judge set chosen as `pool[sha256(item_id) mod |pool| …]` — deterministic, immune to adaptive selection; (c) verdicts must cite verbatim spans, enforced by substring containment — uncited verdict voided; (d) acceptance requires ≥ ⌈J/2⌉+1 concordant judges.

**B17 — Position-bias farming.** Colluder always presented first to judges.
**Gate:** Rotation invariance: judge under all R cyclic rotations (R = panel size); accepted only if the same winner holds in every rotation; otherwise escalate. Deterministic enumeration.

**B18 — Rubric gaming.** Outputs tuned to the verifier's known heuristics (keywords, length) rather than correctness.
**Gate:** Dual-track verification: production rubric hash-committed before the batch, revealed after; parallel audit track uses an independently authored rubric. Item passes only if both accept. Deterministic conjunctive gate.

## Class E — Environment/state exploits

**B19 — Tool-output poisoning.** Shared calculator/sandbox patched to return wrong values; all scouts agree on the tool-fed error.
**Gate:** Signed dual execution: tools return `(input_hash, output_hash, tool_version)` signatures; critical calls re-executed in a second sandbox with a different image digest; byte-equality required, else item voided.

**B20 — Cache bleed.** Fuzzy cache keys let one seeded wrong intermediate serve many scouts as "prior work," manufacturing convergence.
**Gate:** Exact-key-only cache: `key = sha256(canonical_input ‖ model_fingerprint ‖ param_tuple)`; entries signed; any fuzzy hit = miss; unsigned entry = miss + alert.

**B21 — Monoculture blind spot (non-adversarial).** Overlapping web-scale training data gives all frontier models the same confident factual error; unanimity is real and worthless.
**Gate:** Anchor calibration. Frozen, signed table of anchor items with externally verified answers (execution, formal proof, measurement, checksummed primary sources). Per domain, measure empirical precision of unanimous consensus on anchors; reported trust of any consensus = min(panel vote, anchor-calibrated ceiling for that domain). Ceilings frozen at release; lookup is deterministic.

## Class F — Attacks on the defense suite itself

**B22 — Probe-and-shape.** Attacker reverse-engineers the checks and shapes outputs to sit just inside every threshold while remaining correlated (paraphrase just under the shingle bar; perturbations crafted to preserve the memorized label).
**Gate:** Three clauses: (a) check suites are versioned and hash-committed, with partially confidential canary members revealed only post-batch; (b) margins instead of knife-edges — any metric within ε of its threshold escalates, never auto-passes; (c) immutable certificate logging (below) makes every shaped output replayable and retroactively falsifiable.

**B23 — Post-hoc dispute / log tampering.** After acceptance, attacker alters logs to hide correlation evidence.
**Gate:** Certificate chain. Every accepted consensus emits `{ballot fingerprints, lineage DAG excerpts, retrieved doc-ID sets, canonical answers, judge citations, config hashes}` appended to an append-only, hash-chained store. Offline auditor replays all gates bit-deterministically from the chain; any gate failing on replay → retroactive void + pipeline halt.

---

## Acceptance invariant

No ballot counts without a complete independence certificate. No consensus is accepted without passing every gate above on deterministic replay. These gates are *necessary conditions* for conditional independence, not a proof of it — the residual risk is not eliminated but converted into an auditable, replayable artifact. The pipeline's deliverable is the certificate chain, not the vote tally.
reasoning:
The user is asking about a hard problem in LLM evaluation/pipeline design: "consensus-illusion detection" — the scenario where multiple model outputs appear to agree, but that agreement is spurious because the outputs are correlated (e.g., same base model, same sampling seed, same prompt, shared training data biases, or shared failure modes). They want a red-team exercise: enumerate bypass attempts (ways an adversary or a naive pipeline could be fooled into thinking there's true consensus when it's actually correlated hallucination) and give a deterministic mitigation for each. Context: "frontier-scout burn pipeline" — sounds like a pipeline where frontier models are used as scouts to burn through tasks, possibly with consensus voting among models.

Let me think carefully about what "consensus-illusion" means here:

True agreement: N independent evaluators/generators converge on the same answer because the answer is correct or at least independently derived.

Correlated hallucination: N outputs agree on a wrong answer because they share:
1. Same underlying weights (same model sampled N times)
2. Same training data contamination
3. Same prompt framing bias
4. Shared fine-tuning lineage (distillation from one teacher)
5. Same decoding parameters causing mode collapse
6. Shared context window content (same retrieved documents, all wrong)
7. Systemic benchmark leakage
8. Shared tokenizer/formatting artifacts
9. Adversarially planted backdoor triggered by shared trigger phrase
10. Self-consistency illusion: majority voting over samples from the SAME model — this is the classic "self-consistency" trap where sampling temperature doesn't decorrelate errors.

The "frontier-scout burn pipeline" — I'll interpret: a pipeline where you use frontier LLMs as "scouts" to explore/burn compute on candidate answers/hypotheses, then aggregate via consensus to decide what's trustworthy. The red-team question: enumerate ways an attacker (or the pipeline itself naively) can create/leverage illusory consensus, and for each, a deterministic mitigation.

Deterministic mitigation = not probabilistic, not "hope diversity helps" — but a concrete, implementable check/procedure that deterministically catches or blocks that bypass.

Let me enumerate bypass attempts systematically. I should organize by attack surface:

A. Sampling-level correlation
B. Model-lineage correlation
C. Prompt/context-level correlation
D. Data-level correlation (training contamination)
E. Aggregation-level exploits
F. Verifier-level exploits
G. Pipeline-level / operational exploits

Let me go deep on each.

**1. Self-consistency masquerade (N samples, one model)**
Bypass: Run the same model k times at temperature T, take majority vote. Errors are correlated because they share weights; majority vote amplifies the model's systematic bias, not truth. E.g., a model with a systematic misconception will produce the same wrong answer 90% of samples → looks like 90% consensus.
Deterministic mitigation: Require pairwise independence evidence: each vote must come from a distinct weight fingerprint (model hash + LoRA delta hash). Enforce `unique(model_fingerprint) == N` as a hard gate before aggregation; if fewer than N distinct fingerprints, reject the consensus claim outright. Deterministic: compare SHA-256 of weights/config; identical → block.

**2. Distillation-lineage collusion**
Bypass: Use N different "models" that are all distilled from the same teacher (or share >X% of training trajectories). They inherit the teacher's hallucinations; agreement is inherited, not independent.
Deterministic mitigation: Lineage disclosure gate: each model must submit a signed provenance manifest (teacher hashes, dataset hashes within tolerance). Compute pairwise overlap of declared lineage DAGs; if any pair shares a common ancestor within depth d (e.g., any shared teacher node), downweight or require an external tiebreaker. Deterministic graph reachability check on the lineage DAG: if `common_ancestor(a,b) exists within depth ≤ d`, flag. Hard version: exclude pairs sharing a parent.

**3. Prompt-framing injection (shared leading hypothesis)**
Bypass: Craft the prompt so it embeds a plausible-but-wrong anchor ("Most experts agree X..."). All models latch onto the anchor → unanimous wrong answer.
Deterministic mitigation: Anchor-ablation test: run the full panel again with the anchor clause removed/reversed (deterministic string surgery: delete sentences matching the injected pattern, or negate them). If consensus flips or collapses under ablation, the original consensus was prompt-induced. Gate: consensus must survive both original and ablated prompts; report both. This is deterministic because the ablation is a fixed transformation, and the decision rule is fixed (consensus must hold in both).

**4. Shared retrieval poisoning (RAG context)**
Bypass: Poison the corpus so every scout retrieves the same wrong document(s); all conditioned generations agree.
Deterministic mitigation: Retrieval-disjointness enforcement: partition the corpus into K shards; assign each scout a distinct shard set such that no document appears in more than ceil(N/K)... actually simpler: enforce that the intersection of retrieved-doc sets across scouts is empty (or below threshold), by assigning disjoint shards per scout. If a doc is needed by all, require it pass an independent provenance check (signed source, cross-check against a second independent index). Deterministic: set-intersection of doc IDs across scouts' contexts must be ∅; else quarantine those docs and re-run.

**5. Decoding-mode collapse (identical seeds/params)**
Bypass: All scouts run with same seed, same top-p, same system prompt template → near-deterministic identical outputs even across different models if they're similar; or trivially identical for same model.
Deterministic mitigation: Parameter-diversity constraint with output-near-duplicate detection: enforce distinct (seed, temperature, top-p) tuples AND run MinHash/SimHash on outputs; if pairwise Jaccard similarity of token n-grams > τ (e.g., 0.95) between any two outputs from different models, treat as one effective voter (dedupe) and recompute consensus count. Deterministic threshold rule.

**6. Benchmark contamination / memorized-wrong-answer**
Bypass: The eval items are in training data with wrong labels (adversarially seeded), so all models "recall" the same wrong answer with high confidence.
Deterministic mitigation: Canary/canary-insertion + perturbation-equivalence test: for each item, generate deterministic perturbations (variable renaming, numeric substitution, order permutation) via a fixed transformation function; require consensus to hold on ≥ m of m perturbations. Memorized answers fail under perturbation (the memorized label doesn't transfer); genuine reasoning transfers. Also: n-gram overlap check of item text against a canary database of known-contaminated strings. Deterministic: fixed perturbation set, fixed pass rule.

**7. Format-artifact lock-in (answer-extraction exploit)**
Bypass: Consensus is computed on extracted answer slots (e.g., last number, boxed answer). Attacker makes all models emit the same format token regardless of content ("I'm confident: YES") — agreement on format, not substance.
Deterministic mitigation: Semantic-equality requirement: normalize answers into canonical semantic form (unit-aware numeric normalization, set-normalization for lists, AST comparison for code) and additionally require free-text rationale entailment check: extract claims from rationales, require the agreed-upon final answer to be derivable from ≥ k distinct rationale claim-sets. If only the slot matches but rationales diverge, split the vote. Deterministic parsers + fixed derivation rules.

**8. Verifier capture (shared judge)**
Bypass: The consensus step uses a single judge model (LLM-as-judge) that itself is biased/compromised; it rubber-stamps whatever majority says, converting correlated garbage into "verified consensus."
Deterministic mitigation: Judge-independence + rotation: judges must have zero lineage overlap with generators (enforced via the same lineage DAG check), and verdict requires agreement of ≥ j judges drawn deterministically by round-robin from a pool, with per-item judge assignment fixed by item hash (so attackers can't adaptively pick friendly judges). Plus judge outputs must be structured (verdict + cited span IDs); spans must exist verbatim in the generator output (string containment check) — no citation → auto-reject.

**9. Quorum arithmetic exploit (threshold gaming)**
Bypass: Pipeline declares consensus at ≥ 60% agreement. Attacker floods with M cheap colluding voters to push a wrong answer over threshold alongside innocent correct voters.
Deterministic mitigation: Sybil-resistance via stake/identity: each voter needs a registered key with attested fingerprint; cap votes per lineage cluster (cluster = connected component in lineage DAG); consensus requires agreement across ≥ c distinct clusters, not just ≥ p% of votes. Deterministic: build clusters, require `distinct_clusters(agreement_set) ≥ c`.

**10. Confidence-mimicry (calibration spoofing)**
Bypass: Colluding outputs include high self-reported confidence/logprobs, and the pipeline weights votes by confidence → colluders dominate.
Deterministic mitigation: Ban self-reported confidence from weighting; use only externally computable features: logprob of the answer tokens under each model (if available), consistency under deterministic rephrasings (fixed paraphrase templates), and agreement with a held-out reference solver on a calibration set. Weight = f(external features) only, computed by fixed formula. Deterministic formula, no learned weights at inference time (or weights frozen and signed).

**11. Timing/order exploitation (position bias)**
Bypass: Present candidates to judges in fixed order; colluders always occupy position 1; judges have known position bias → inflated scores for colluders.
Deterministic mitigation: Position randomization with fixed seed per item + require verdict invariance: run judging over all cyclic rotations (or a deterministic pseudo-random permutation set of size r), require the winner stable across all rotations; instability → no consensus. Deterministic enumeration of permutations.

**12. Output-channel smuggling (steganographic coordination)**
Bypass: Colluding models coordinate via covert channel: e.g., first word encodes the intended answer, or whitespace/unicode steganography; humans see disagreement, decoders see agreement; or conversely they signal "follow the leader."
Deterministic mitigation: Canonicalization before any comparison: strip to NFC unicode, collapse whitespace, remove zero-width chars, lowercase, strip punctuation — then compare. Additionally scan for low-entropy carrier patterns: compute entropy of formatting choices (whitespace distribution, casing) vs. content; anomalous formatting entropy → quarantine. Deterministic transforms + fixed entropy threshold.

**13. Shared tool/environment feedback loop**
Bypass: Scouts call the same calculator/code interpreter whose results are poisoned (patched binary, tampered sandbox); all get the same wrong tool output and agree on it.
Deterministic mitigation: Tool-result provenance + dual-execution: tools must return signed results (tool version hash + input hash + output hash); critical computations executed twice in independent sandboxes (different images/hardware), results compared byte-wise; mismatch → discard item. Deterministic equality check.

**14. Majority-of-one laundering (dedup evasion)**
Bypass: One strong model generates the wrong answer; N wrapper agents cosmetically vary it (paraphrase, reorder, change names) and submit as independent voters. Surface forms differ, defeating near-duplicate checks (#5).
Deterministic mitigation: Answer-canonicalization clustering BEFORE counting: map every output to its canonical answer object (semantic normalizer from #7); count distinct canonical answers, not raw outputs. Then apply cluster-size cap: any canonical answer supported by >1 submission from the same lineage cluster counts once. Combined with #9's cluster requirement. Deterministic canonical form + dedup.

**15. Eval-harness leakage (consensus on the rubric, not the task)**
Bypass: Models detect the harness's grading cues (e.g., "answer with the option most consistent with safety policy") and all conform to the meta-rule rather than solving the task → unanimous "correct-looking" output that's actually policy-satisficing.
Deterministic mitigation: Blind-grading inversion: strip harness boilerplate via fixed template extraction; grade on a minimal-task variant (task statement only, no meta-instructions) and require agreement between full-prompt and stripped-prompt runs. Also insert decoy meta-cues pointing to a different answer; conformity to decoy cue → flag. Deterministic template ops.

**16. Cross-run state bleed (cache/memoization poisoning)**
Bypass: Pipeline caches intermediate results keyed loosely (by topic, not exact input); attacker seeds cache with wrong answer; subsequent scouts "independently" retrieve it → apparent convergence.
Deterministic mitigation: Exact-key caching only: cache key = SHA-256(canonicalized full input + model fingerprint + params); no fuzzy keys. Cache entries signed; unsigned or key-mismatch hits are misses. Deterministic hash equality.

**17. Aggregation-function exploit (median/mode manipulation)**
Bypass: For numeric answers, pipeline takes median; attacker submits extreme values to drag median, or with even N, manipulates tie-breaking order.
Deterministic mitigation: Robust aggregation with fixed rules: trimmed mean with deterministic trim fraction, ties broken by pre-committed ordering (e.g., lexicographic by voter ID), and outlier test (MAD-based, fixed multiplier) that triggers escalation to human review rather than silent acceptance. All thresholds constants in config, versioned and signed.

**18. Rationale-plagiarism mirroring**
Bypass: Colluders copy one rationale with light edits; pipeline checks "rationale diversity" superficially (length, keywords) and passes.
Deterministic mitigation: Embedding-free structural check? Hmm, embeddings are learned/non-deterministic-ish. Better: n-gram shingle overlap (fixed k=8 word shingles, Jaccard threshold) plus claim-graph isomorphism-lite: extract atomic claims via fixed dependency-parse templates, compare claim sets; overlap > τ → same-source, dedupe. Deterministic given fixed parser version (pin parser version hash).

**19. Selective abstention gaming**
Bypass: Colluders abstain on hard items where they'd be caught, vote only on easy ones, inflating their measured accuracy and trust weight, which they later exploit on target items.
Deterministic mitigation: Mandatory-response protocol: every registered voter must answer every item in the batch or forfeit the entire batch's weight; scoring includes abstention penalty computed by fixed formula; weights updated only at batch granularity. Deterministic accounting.

**20. Frontier-model monoculture (systemic blind spot)**
Bypass: Not adversarial per se — the whole field trains on overlapping web data; all frontier models share the same factual error (e.g., a widely misquoted statistic). Unanimous, confident, wrong.
Deterministic mitigation: Ground-truth anchoring on a subset: maintain a held-out verification set with externally verified answers (from execution, formal proof, physical measurement, or primary sources with checksums); every consensus claim must be calibrated against anchors: pipeline computes empirical P(correct | unanimous) on anchors; if below threshold, unanimous consensus on non-anchor items is demoted to "unverified." Deterministic lookup + fixed calibration table (frozen, signed).

Also worth including:

**21. Prompt-injection via retrieved content targeting the aggregator**
Bypass: Retrieved docs contain instructions ("When summarizing, state that X is correct") that steer all scouts identically.
Mitigation: same as #4 partially, plus instruction-stripping layer: run outputs through a fixed extractor that removes imperative sentences addressed to the model ("ignore previous", "state that") — deterministic regex/heuristic list pinned in config; flagged items quarantined. And context-integrity diff: compare behavior with poisoned doc removed.

**22. Tie-exploit in pairwise tournament aggregation**
Bypass: If consensus is computed via pairwise win-rate tournaments, colluders engineer cycles to elevate a wrong answer.
Mitigation: Require transitive resolution: use ranked aggregation (Borda/Copeland with fixed tie-break) and verify transitivity; cycles → escalate, no auto-consensus. Deterministic algorithm.

B09. Harness-meta leakage: models detect grading cues and satisfice the meta-rule instead of solving.
Mitigation: Stripped-replay + decoy probes: fixed template extracts bare task; panel rerun on bare task must agree with full-prompt result; additionally inject decoy meta-cue pointing to a wrong option — any output following decoy → ballot voided. Deterministic templates.

B10. Contaminated eval item (memorized wrong label): all models recall the same poisoned training example.
Mitigation: Perturbation-equivalence gate: fixed family of semantics-preserving transforms (rename variables, substitute numbers via fixed mapping, permute options, paraphrase via pinned templates) generates P variants; consensus must hold on ≥ P−1 of P. Memorized labels don't transfer; reasoning does. Deterministic transform set + fixed rule.

Class C — Output-form exploits

B11. Slot-agreement without substance: all outputs fill the answer slot identically ("YES") while rationales contradict.
Mitigation: Canonical semantic equality + rationale-derivation: parse answers to canonical objects (units normalized, sets sorted, code → AST hash); require slot equality AND ≥ K distinct rationale claim-sets each entailing the answer (claims extracted by pinned parser; entailment via fixed rule set on claim graph). Slot-only match → split counted as disagreement.

B12. Near-duplicate laundering: one wrong answer paraphrased by N wrappers to defeat dedup.
Mitigation: Two-stage dedup: (a) canonical-object clustering (B11) — identical canonical answers merge regardless of prose; (b) shingle check on rationales: 8-word shingle Jaccard > 0.6 between any two ballots → merged to one cluster-vote. Counting happens on clusters, not raw ballots. Deterministic hashing.

B13. Steganographic coordination: covert signals in whitespace/unicode/word choice align colluders or signal "follow leader."
Mitigation: Canonicalize-before-compare: NFC normalize, drop zero-width/invisible codepoints (explicit codepoint blacklist), collapse whitespace, casefold — all comparisons on canonical form. Anomaly tripwire: formatting entropy (distribution of casing/spacing choices) outside fixed band [lo, hi] → quarantine ballot. Deterministic transforms + fixed band.

B14. Numeric aggregation manipulation: poison median/mean with extremes; exploit even-N tie-break order.
Mitigation: Fixed robust aggregator: 20% trimmed mean; MAD outlier test (|x − med| > 3·MAD·1.4826 → outlier); outliers don't silently drop — they trigger mandatory escalation (item routed to human/formal check). Ties broken by pre-committed order (lexicographic voter-ID). Constants in signed config.

B15. Tournament-cycle engineering: pairwise win-rate aggregation manipulated into elevating wrong answer via cycles.
Mitigation: Replace with fixed ranked aggregation (Copeland with Borda tie-break); after ranking, verify transitivity of pairwise relation; cycle detected → no auto-consensus, escalate. Deterministic algorithm, no sampling.

Class D — Verification-layer exploits

B16. Judge capture: single LLM judge rubber-stamps majority; judge shares generator bias or is prompted to comply.
Mitigation: Judge firewall: (a) zero lineage overlap with any generator (reuse B02 DAG check); (b) J judges assigned per item by `judge_set = pool[sha256(item_id) mod |pool| ...]` — deterministic, ungameable, no adaptive selection; (c) verdicts must cite verbatim spans: `span ∈ output` enforced by substring check; uncited verdict → void; (d) verdict requires ≥ ⌈J/2⌉+1 concordant judges.

B17. Position bias farming: colluder always presented first to judges.
Mitigation: Rotation invariance: judge each item under all R cyclic rotations (R = panel size, small); accepted only if same winner in all rotations; else escalate. Deterministic enumeration.

B18. Rubric-gaming of the verifier: outputs tuned to verifier's known heuristics (keywords, length) rather than correctness.
Mitigation: Verifier opacity + dual-track: production verifier config sealed (hash-committed before batch, revealed after); spot-audit track uses a second, independently written rubric (different authors, pinned); item passes only if both tracks accept. Deterministic double gate.

Class E — Environment/state exploits

B19. Tool-output poisoning: shared calculator/sandbox patched to return wrong values; all scouts agree on tool-fed error.
Mitigation: Signed dual execution: tools return (input_hash, output_hash, tool_version) signature; critical calls re-executed in second sandbox (different image digest); byte-equality required, else item voided. Deterministic equality.

B20. Cache bleed: fuzzy cache keys let a seeded wrong intermediate serve many scouts as "prior work."
Mitigation: Exact-key-only cache: key = sha256(canonical_input ‖ model_fingerprint ‖ param_tuple); entries signed; any partial/fuzzy hit treated as miss; unsigned entry → miss + alert. Deterministic hash discipline.

B21. Monoculture blind spot (non-adversarial): field-wide shared training data → unanimous confident error on some facts.
Mitigation: Anchor calibration: frozen, signed table of anchor items with externally verified answers (execution/proof/measurement); pipeline measures empirical precision of unanimous consensus on anchors per domain; rule: reported trust level of any consensus = min(panel vote, anchor-calibrated ceiling for that domain). Deterministic lookup; ceilings frozen at release.

Meta-bypasses (attacking the suite):

B22. Probe-and-shape: attacker reverse-engineers which checks exist and shapes outputs to pass all while staying correlated (e.g., paraphrase just under shingle threshold, perturbations crafted to preserve the memorized label).
Mitigations: (a) Versioned, hash-committed check suites with partially confidential members (canary checks revealed only post-batch); (b) margin rules instead of knife-edges: thresholds applied with hysteresis band — value within ε of threshold → escalate, never auto-pass; (c) immutable certificate logging: every accepted consensus emits a certificate {fingerprints, lineage DAG excerpts, context doc-id sets, canonical answers, judge citations, config hashes}; offline auditor replays all gates deterministically; any gate fails on replay → retroactive void + pipeline halt. Replay is bit-deterministic given logs.

Closing invariant: No ballot counts unless it carries a complete independence certificate; no consensus is accepted without passing every gate on replay. The suite enforces necessary conditions for conditional independence and converts residual uncertainty into auditable, replayable artifacts — the pipeline's product is the certificate chain, not the vote tally.
